The company had frozen new hiring, but Ujjwal did not want to wait for an opening. He asked Zubin, his manager, for ten minutes at the end of a crowded Thursday with two deadlines looming.

"I'd like to join the analytics project for the sales team," Ujjwal said. "I already do the monthly reports, so I know the data. I'd take the extra work on top of my own, just for a quarter."

Zubin sighed. "We're stretched, and I can't promise a formal move." He paused. "But Priya's group could use someone for the dashboards. I'll ask."

On Monday Ujjwal was pulled into the first meeting. It wasn't a new job, but it was one step closer to the field he wanted.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal already do for the company?
How did Ujjwal feel while asking Zubin, and what shows it?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt determined but somewhat nervous, since he chose a busy Thursday and offered to take on extra work to make the request easier to accept.

qa.q: What could Ujjwal do if the analytics project turned out not to lead to a formal move, and why?
qa.a: Ujjwal could use the experience to build a portfolio and apply for openings elsewhere, because the skills gained still count toward the new field.

qa.q: How might Zubin see Ujjwal's request during a hiring freeze?
qa.a: Zubin is stretched and cannot promise a move, but may welcome a motivated team member who offers to help the analytics group.

Pema had spent two years in customer operations at a Bengaluru logistics company, and for the last six months she'd been teaching herself data analysis at night.
One Thursday she noticed an email: the analytics team was starting a project on late deliveries. She read it twice, then booked fifteen minutes with her manager, Anand.
"I'd like to help on that project," she said. "I know the complaint data better than anyone, I've been learning spreadsheets and queries, and I could spend two days a week on it."
Anand frowned. "Who handles your queue those days?"
"I've spoken to Farah. She'll cover Tuesday and Wednesday, and I'll take her Saturday shift."
Anand thought, then nodded. "Three months. Then we see."
In her first week Pema found that two delivery zones caused half of the complaints. The analytics lead asked her to present it on Friday.

qa.q: Who agreed to cover Pema's queue?
qa.a: Farah agreed to cover Tuesday and Wednesday.

qa.q: How did Pema likely feel when she read the email about the project?
qa.a: She likely felt excited but nervous, reading it twice before booking time with her manager.

qa.q: What else could Pema do to make the most of the three months?
qa.a: She could ask the analytics lead for feedback regularly, so she knows which skills to build for a full move later.

qa.q: How does the request look from Anand's side?
qa.a: Anand's main worry is who covers her queue, and once that is answered, he sees a low-risk trial that uses her knowledge of the data.

grounding: Shows the person asking the manager to join an analytics project inside the same company, using transferable skills as a bridge to a new field.

"Zainab, can I have five minutes?" Harish stood by the door of her cabin.
"Sure. Sit."
"I've heard the pricing team needs someone for the new analytics project."
"They do. You're on sales, Harish."
"Yes. But I've built all our monthly sales reports for two years. I know where every number comes from. And I've been doing an evening course in data analysis." He put a folder on her desk. "These are two dashboards I made from our own sales data."
Zainab flipped through them. "These are decent. What about your targets?"
"I'd still handle my key accounts. Could I give the project two afternoons a week for three months?"
"If your numbers dip, you're back full-time."
"Fair."
"I'll talk to the pricing head today." She closed the folder. "Honestly, Harish, it's easier to take a chance on someone we already know."

qa.q: How many afternoons a week did Harish ask to give the project?
qa.a: He asked to give the project two afternoons a week.

qa.q: How did Harish feel standing at the door, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He was probably nervous but prepared, asking for five minutes and bringing a folder of dashboards to show.

qa.q: What else could Harish do to show he's ready for a full move?
qa.a: He could keep his sales numbers steady and document what he contributes to the pricing project, so the next step is based on results.

qa.q: How does the request look from Zainab's side?
qa.a: Zainab sees a low-risk move with someone she already knows and trusts, as long as his sales targets don't slip.
